implementation: Flutter login now accepts any nonempty password, matching the web form and login API for existing accounts. Registration alone enforces the backend contract of 12–128 Unicode code points.

checks.name: Short existing password is submitted for login
checks.command: flutter test test/auth_screen_test.dart --plain-name "login submits a shorter existing password"
checks.observation: A nonempty password shorter than 12 characters reaches /api/v1/auth/login with the entered value.

checks.name: Registration rejects password below minimum
checks.command: flutter test test/auth_screen_test.dart --plain-name "registration enforces server password length limits"
checks.observation: An 11-character password is rejected locally and no request is sent.

checks.name: Registration rejects password above maximum
checks.command: flutter test test/auth_screen_test.dart --plain-name "registration enforces server password length limits"
checks.observation: A 129-code-point password is rejected locally and no request is sent.

remaining: Physical Samsung/Gboard multi-character input and native validation/error/focus behavior remain open device acceptance; widget tests do not verify a real IME.
